full_judgment:
2. The plaintiffs filed S.C.C. Suit No. 11 of 1972 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Sylhet exercising jurisdiction of the judge under the S.C.C. Act for evicting the defendant from the premises described in the schedule to the plaint by removing the structures and for recovery of khas possession, on the allegations, inter alia, that the defendant was a defaulter and that he constructed a pucca building without the consent of the plaintiffs who bonafide require the premises. 

 "(1) That the puffs, have filed the aforesaid suit for eviction of the defdt. from the suit premises removing all obstruction and for khas possession. 

 "Evicting the defdt. from the premises described in the schedule below by removing all obstructions and for recovery of khas possession." 

 6. This prayer discloses that the plaintiffs do not pray for a declaration of their title. A suit for ejectment of the defendant by removing obstructions and for recovery of khas possession, in all circumstances may not depend on a question of proof or disproof of a Title to the immovable properly. In the instant case the plaintiffs do not appear to have claimed the relief depending on proof or dis-proof of a title to the immovable properly. Mr. Matin submits that in a suit under the S.C.C. jurisdiction, the Court may enquire into the question of title. The learned Advocate has referred to a decision in the case of Dr. Habibur Rahman and another Vs. Md. Mansur reported in 25 D.L.R. (Dacca) 211 in support of the proposition. There is no dispute with the proposition laid therein. Unless the plaintiffs framed the suit for a declaration of title with other necessary consequential reliefs, the mere enquiry into the question of title, will not, by itself, convert the suit into a suit for title depending on proof or disproof of title to immovable properly. The provision in section 23(1) of the S.C.C. Act clearly indicates that the Court had jurisdiction to return the plaint at any stage of the proceeding. This is merely directory and not mandatory. It is evident from the expression "the Court may at any stage of the proceedings return the plaint". On a perusal of the impugned order, it oboes appear that the defendant raised any objection to the plaintiff's prayer. It was not contended before the learned S.C.C. Judge that the relief claimed in the suit depended on the proof or disproof of title to the immovable property. In the circumstances, the court was rot called upon to direct its attention whether or net the relief claimed in the suit depended upon proof or disproof of title to immovable properly and consequently the court was not required to record any finding in that behalf. Therefore, it cannot be concluded that it was the duty of the court to return the plaint if, in its opinion, the relief claimed by the plaintiffs in a suit depended upon the proof or disproof of a title to immovable property or other title which such a court cannot finally determine. In the instant case the learned Munsif has allowed the application in the interest of justice. The averments made in the application dated 10.9.73 clearly indicate that the suit was filed in S.C.C. jurisdiction through inadvertence and that "the matter in issue involved" warrants for an adjudication of the same in a title suit. From this statement, the relief claimed in 'the suit was not changed. The suit with its relief as contained in paragraph 14 remained as before. Thus the transfer, in the interest of justice, cannot be construed to be an act rot contemplated by the provisions of the S.C.C. Act or that the same was without jurisdiction. It may be pointed out that the learned Munsif in whose court the suit, in the S.C.C. Jurisdiction was filed is the court with ordinary Civil Jurisdiction relating to the case. It could not be pointed out on the strength of any authority that the order complained of was without jurisdiction.
